The the value of $r$ is ______
questions.solution:
For $\mathrm{x}=1 \left(1+\frac{2}{5}\right)^{23}=a_0+a_1+a_2+\ldots+a_{23}$
for numerically greatest term

questions.q: Let $a$ and $b$ be two nonzero real numbers. If the coefficient of ${x}^{5}$ in the expansion of ${\left(a{x}^{2} + \dfrac{70}{27bx}\right)}^{4}$ is equal to the coefficient of ${x}^{- 5}$ in the expansion of ${\left(ax - \dfrac{1}{b{x}^{2}}\right)}^{7}$, then the value of $2b$ is
questions.solution:
Given,

The coefficient of ${x}^{5}$ in ${\left(a{x}^{2} + \dfrac{70}{27bx}\right)}^{4}$ is equal to coefficient of ${x}^{- 5}$ in ${\left(ax - \dfrac{1}{b{x}^{2}}\right)}^{7}$,

Now finding the coefficient of ${x}^{5}$ in ${\left(a{x}^{2} + \dfrac{70}{27bx}\right)}^{4}$ we get,

${T}_{r + 1} = Cr 4 {\left(a{x}^{2}\right)}^{4 - r} \cdot {\left(\dfrac{70}{27bx}\right)}^{r}$

$⇒ {T}_{r + 1} = Cr 4 {\left(a\right)}^{4 - r} \cdot {\left(\dfrac{70}{27b}\right)}^{r} \cdot {x}^{8 - 2r - r}$

So, $8 - 2r - r = 5 ⇒ r = 1$

So, ${T}_{2} = C1 4 {a}^{3} \cdot \dfrac{70}{27b} \cdot {x}^{5}$

Now finding the coefficient of ${x}^{- 5}$ in ${\left(ax - \dfrac{1}{b{x}^{2}}\right)}^{7}$ we get,

${T}_{r + 1} = Cr 7 {\left(ax\right)}^{7 - r} \cdot {\left(\dfrac{1}{b{x}^{2}}\right)}^{r}$

$⇒ {T}_{r + 1} = Cr 7 {\left(a\right)}^{7 - r} \cdot {\left(\dfrac{1}{b}\right)}^{r} \cdot {x}^{7 - r - 2r}$

So, $7 - r - 2r = - 5 ⇒ r = 4$

So, ${T}_{5} = C4 7 {\left(a\right)}^{3} \cdot {\left(\dfrac{1}{b}\right)}^{4} \cdot {x}^{- 5}$

Now equating the coefficient of ${x}^{5} \text{ and } {x}^{- 5}$ we get,

$C4 7 {\left(a\right)}^{3} \cdot {\left(\dfrac{1}{b}\right)}^{4} = C1 4 {a}^{3} \cdot \dfrac{70}{27b}$

$⇒ 35{a}^{3} \cdot {\left(\dfrac{1}{b}\right)}^{4} = 4{a}^{3} \cdot \dfrac{70}{27b}$

$⇒ {\left(\dfrac{1}{b}\right)}^{3} = 4 \times \dfrac{2}{27}$

$⇒ b = \dfrac{3}{2} ⇒ 2b = 3$

questions.q:
For nonnegative integers $s$ and $r$, let $\left(\begin{array}{ll}s \\ r\end{array}\right) = \left\{\begin{cases}\dfrac{s !}{r ! \left(s - r\right) !} & \text{if}r \le s \\ 0 & \text{if}r > s\end{cases}\right$. For positive integers $m$ and $n,$ let $g\left(m, n\right) = \mathop{∑}_{p = 0}^{m + n}\dfrac{f\left(m, n, p\right)}{\left(\begin{array}{ll}n + p \\ p\end{array}\right)}$, where for any nonnegative integer $p$,
$f\left(m, n, p\right) = \mathop{∑}_{i = 0}^{p}\left(\begin{array}{ll}m \\ i\end{array}\right)\left(\begin{array}{ll}n + i \\ p\end{array}\right)\left(\begin{array}{ll}p + n \\ p - i\end{array}\right)$. Then which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
options: $g\left(m, n\right) = g\left(n, m\right)$ for all positive integers $m, n$
$g\left(m, n + 1\right) = g\left(m + 1, n\right)$ for all positive integers $m, n$
$g\left(2m, 2n\right) = 2g\left(m, n\right)$ for all positive integers $m, n$
$g\left(2m, 2n\right) = {\left(g\left(m, n\right)\right)}^{2}$ for all positive intergers $m, n$
questions.solution:
$f\left(m, n, p\right) = \mathop{∑}_{i = 0}^{p}\left(\begin{array}{ll}m \\ i\end{array}\right)\left(\begin{array}{ll}n + i \\ p\end{array}\right)\left(\begin{array}{ll}p + n \\ p - i\end{array}\right)$

$= \mathop{∑}_{i = 0}^{p} Ci m \cdot \dfrac{\left(n + i\right) !}{p ! \left(n + i - p\right) !} \cdot \dfrac{( p + n ) !}{\left(p - i\right) ! \left(n + i\right) !}$

$= \mathop{∑}_{i = 0}^{p} Ci m \cdot \dfrac{( p + n ) !}{p ! n !} \cdot \dfrac{n !}{\left(n + i - p\right) ! \left(p - i\right) !}$

$= \mathop{∑}_{i = 0}^{p} Ci m . Cp p + n \cdot Cp - i n$

$Cp p + n \cdot \mathop{∑}_{i = 0}^{p} Ci m \cdot Cp - i n$

$\left(∵ \mathop{∑}_{i = 0}^{p} Ci m \cdot Cp - i n = Cp m + n\right)$

$∴ f\left(m, n, p\right) = Cp p + n . Cp m + n$

$⇒ \dfrac{f\left(m, n, p\right)}{Cp p + n} = Cp m + n$.

$g\left(m, n\right) = \mathop{∑}_{p = 0}^{m + n} Cp m + n = {2}^{m + n}$

(A) $g ( 2m, 2n ) = {2}^{2m + 2n}$

$2g\left(m, n\right) = 2 . {2}^{m + n}$

(B) $g\left(m, n + 1\right) = {2}^{m + n + 1} = g\left(m + 1, n\right)$

(C) $g\left(2m, 2n\right) = {2}^{2m + 2n} = {\left({2}^{m + n}\right)}^{2} = {\left(g\left(m, n\right)\right)}^{2}$

(D) $g\left(m, n\right) = g\left(n, m\right)$.

questions.solution:
As given $\left|\begin{cases}\mathop{∑}_{k = 0}^{n} k & \mathop{∑}_{k = 0}^{n} C n {}_{k} {k}^{2} \\ \mathop{∑}_{k = 0}^{n} C n {}_{k} k & \mathop{∑}_{k = 0}^{n} C n {}_{k} {3}^{k}\end{cases}\right| = 0$
$\left(a\right)\mathop{∑}_{k = 0}^{n}k =\dfrac{n\left(n + 1\right)}{2}$
$\left(b\right)\mathop{∑}_{k = 0}^{n}{C}_{k} n \left({k}^{2}\right) = \mathop{∑}_{k = 0}^{n}{\left({k}^{2} - k + k\right)}^{n}{C}_{k}$
$= \mathop{∑}_{k = 0}^{n}\left({k}^{2} - k\right) {C}_{k} n + \mathop{∑}_{k = 0}^{n}k {C}_{k} n$
$= \mathop{∑}_{k = 0}^{n}k\left(k - 1\right)\dfrac{n}{k} . \dfrac{n - 1}{k - 1} {C}_{k - 2} n - 2 + \mathop{∑}_{k = 0}^{n}k\dfrac{n}{k} {C}_{k - 1} n - 1$
$= n\left(n - 1\right)\mathop{∑}_{k = 0}^{n}{C}_{k - 2} n - 2 + n\mathop{∑}_{k = 0}^{n}{C}_{k - 1} n - 1$
$= n\left(n - 1\right){2}^{n - 2} + n{2}^{n - 1} = n{2}^{n - 2}\left(n - 1 + 2\right) = n\left(n + 1\right){2}^{n - 2}$
$\left(\begin{array}{ll}∴ r {C}_{r} n = n {C}_{r - 1} n - 1 \\ ∴ \mathop{∑}_{r = 0}^{n}{C}_{r} n = {2}^{n}\end{array}$\right)$
\left(c\right)\mathop{∑}_{k = 0}^{n}{C}_{k} n k = \mathop{∑}_{k = 0}^{n}k {C}_{k} n = \mathop{∑}_{k = 0}^{n}k\dfrac{n}{k} {C}_{k - 1} n - 1$
$= n\mathop{∑}_{k = 0}^{n}{C}_{k - 1} n - 1 = n{2}^{n - 1}$
$\left(d\right)$\mathop{∑}_{k = 0}^{n}{C}_{k} n {3}^{k} = {C}_{0} n + {C}_{1}3 + {C}_{2} n {3}^{2} + \ldots + {C}_{n} n {3}^{n} n$
$= {$\left(1 + 3\right)$}^{n}$
$= {4}^{n}$
now \left|\begin{cases}\dfrac{n\left(n + 1\right)}{2} & n \left(n + 1\right){2}^{n - 2} \\ n{2}^{n - 1} & {4}^{n}\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$n\left(n + 1\right){2}^{2n - 1} - {n}^{2}\left(n + 1\right){2}^{2n - 3} = 0$

${2}^{2n - 1} - n{2}^{2n - 3} = 0$
$n = 4$
Now $\mathop{∑}_{k = 0}^{4}\dfrac{{C}_{k} 4}{k + 1} = \dfrac{1}{5}\mathop{∑}_{k = 0}^{4}{C}_{k + 1} 5$
$\begin{cases}= \dfrac{1}{5}\left({2}^{5} - 1\right)$ & $\left(∴ \dfrac{{C}_{r} n}{r + 1} = \dfrac{{C}_{r + 1} n + 1}{n + 1}\right)$\end{cases}$
$\begin{cases}= $\dfrac{31}{5} =$6.20 & $\left(∴ \mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{n}{C}_{r} = {2}^{r} - 1 n\right)$\end{cases}$

$

questions.q: The coefficients of three consecutive terms of& ${\left(1 + \text{x}\right)}^{\text{n} + 5}$ are in the ratio $\text{5 : 10 : 14}$. Then $\text{n} =$
questions.solution:
$\text{n} + 5{\text{C}}_{\text{r} - 1}\text{:}\text{n} + 5{\text{C}}_{\text{r}}\text{:}\text{n} + 5{\text{C}}_{\text{r} + 1} = \text{5 : 10 :14}$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(n + 5\right) !}{\left(r - 1\right) ! \left(n - r + 6\right) !}: \dfrac{\left(n + 5\right) !}{\left(r\right) ! \left(n - r + 5\right) !}: \dfrac{\left(n + 5\right) !}{\left(r + 1\right) ! \left(n - r + 4\right) !} = \text{5 : 10 :14}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{\left(r - 1\right) ! \left(n - r + 6\right) !}: \dfrac{1}{\left(r\right) ! \left(n - r + 5\right) !}: \dfrac{1}{\left(r + 1\right) ! \left(n - r + 4\right) !} = \text{5 : 10 :14}$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(r + 1\right)r}{\left(n - r + 6\right) !}: \dfrac{r + 1}{\left(n - r + 5\right) !}: \dfrac{1}{\left(n - r + 4\right) !} = \text{5 : 10 :14}$

$⇒ \left(r + 1\right)r: \left(r + 1\right)\left(n - r + 6\right): \left(n - r + 6\right)\left(n - r + 5\right) = \text{5 : 10 :14}$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(r + 1\right)\left(n - r + 6\right)}{\left(r + 1\right)r} = \dfrac{10}{5}\text{and}\dfrac{\left(n - r + 6\right)\left(n - r + 5\right)}{\left(r + 1\right)\left(n - r + 6\right)} = \dfrac{14}{10}$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(n - r + 6\right)}{r} = 2\text{and}\dfrac{\left(n - r + 5\right)}{\left(r + 1\right)} = \dfrac{7}{5}$

$⇒ n = 3r - 6\text{and}\text{n} = \dfrac{12r - 18}{5}$

$⇒ 3r - 6 = \dfrac{12r - 18}{5} = n$

$⇒ 15r - 30 = 12r - 18$

$⇒ r = 4$

$⇒ n = 6$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(r + 1\right)r}{\left(n - r + 6\right) !}: \dfrac{r + 1}{\left(n - r + 5\right) !}: \dfrac{1}{\left(n - r + 4\right) !} = \text{5 : 10 :14}$

$⇒ \left(r + 1\right)r: \left(r + 1\right)\left(n - r + 6\right): \left(n - r + 6\right)\left(n - r + 5\right) = \text{5 : 10 :14}$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(r + 1\right)\left(n - r + 6\right)}{\left(r + 1\right)r} = \dfrac{10}{5}\text{and}\dfrac{\left(n - r + 6\right)\left(n - r + 5\right)}{\left(r + 1\right)\left(n - r + 6\right)} = \dfrac{14}{10}$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(n - r + 6\right)}{r} = 2\text{and}\dfrac{\left(n - r + 5\right)}{\left(r + 1\right)} = \dfrac{7}{5}$

$⇒ n = 3r - 6\text{and}\text{n} = \dfrac{12r - 18}{5}$

$⇒ 3r - 6 = \dfrac{12r - 18}{5} = n$

$⇒ 15r - 30 = 12r - 18$

$⇒ r = 4$

$⇒ n = 6$
